sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values
sources.licence: project contribution under the repository's terms

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the nightshades work (2026-10-17): every character from the floras in the nightshades notes (plantgen-claude project-files/nightshades/SOURCES.md), drawn by the rules its taxa hold; drawing values only where no character says them.

taxon.note: WCVP v16 accepted name Atropa bella-donna, plant_name_id 2665943 (Library 1.0 list, read 2026-10-17).

growth_form.note: Its habit as the floras describe it, drawn by the forb form.

growth.note: Grown to the age it is drawn at: an annual's one season, a perennial's or shrub's few years.

variants.note: One seed in the open, as the built-in species.

generator.params.note: Drawing values no character gives (nightshades, 2026-10-17): three stems from the stout rootstock (Hooker p. 287) by eye from photographs (iNaturalist 114160319); stem 14 mm at the foot; six leaves below the first fork, by eye.

traits.life_span.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 331 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): a perennial herb with a thick, creeping root; the stems annual.

traits.perennation.note: Hooker, Student's Flora, 3rd ed. (1884), Atropa, p. 287 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): rootstock stout, fleshy and stoloniferous.

traits.height_typical_m.note: Hooker, Student's Flora, 3rd ed. (1884), Atropa, p. 287 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): stem 2-3 ft; King's (vol. 1 p. 331): about 3 ft; Wikipedia 'Atropa bella-donna': up to 2 m, more commonly 1.5 m.

traits.sympodium.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 331 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): stems branching by forking (dichotomously); Hooker p. 288: flowers in the forks or the axils.

traits.sympodial_unit_leaves.note: Two leaves, the pair, on each unit between forks, from photographs (iNaturalist 133257326); no source read this session counts them.

traits.leaves_geminate.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 331 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves mostly two together, unequal; Hooker p. 287: usually in unequal pairs; Bentham p. 319: a smaller leaf usually from the same point.

traits.leaf_shape.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 331 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): leaves ovate, acute, entire; the Pharmacopoeia's broadly ovate (p. 332).

traits.leaf_margin.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 331 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): entire.

traits.leaf_apex.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 332 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): tapering at the tip (Pharmacopoeia); Kilmer: acute or acuminate.

traits.leaf_base_shape.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 332 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): narrowing evenly into the petiole (Pharmacopoeia); Hooker: the larger narrowed into the petiole.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 332 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): 10-15 cm long, 5-10 cm broad (Pharmacopoeia); Hooker: the larger 3-8 in.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 332 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): 5-10 cm broad.

traits.leaf_colour.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 331 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): soft, dull green. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.inflorescence.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 331 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): flowers solitary, stalked, drooping; Bentham p. 319: solitary on short peduncles in the forks or axils.

traits.corolla_shape.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 331 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): corolla campanulate, with a short tube and 5 shallow, nearly equal lobes.

traits.flower_posture.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 331 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): flowers drooping; Hooker p. 288: drooping; Bailey (vol. 1 p. 428): nodding on lateral peduncles.

traits.bark_colour.note: iNaturalist observation 133257326 (CC-licensed photograph, viewed 2026-10-17): the stems are green, purplish in the sun. No text read gives it.

traits.flower_size_m.note: Hooker, Student's Flora, 3rd ed. (1884), Atropa, p. 288 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): corolla 1 in long; Bentham: nearly an inch. Drawn as the bell's length.

traits.flower_colour.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 331 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): dark dull purple at the rim, paler toward the base; Hooker: greenish purple. The colour is our reading of the words.

traits.petal_apex.note: Hooker, Student's Flora, 3rd ed. (1884), Atropa, p. 288 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): lobes subequal, spreading, blunt.

traits.fruit_type.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 331 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): a 2-celled, many-seeded berry on the enlarged calyx.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Wikipedia, 'Atropa bella-donna' (read 2026-10-17): berries about 1.5 cm across; Bentham: rather large and globular.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Wikipedia, 'Atropa bella-donna' (read 2026-10-17): green berries ripen shiny black (Bailey vol. 1 p. 428 says purple). The colour is our reading of the word.

traits.flowering_months.note: Hooker, Student's Flora, 3rd ed. (1884), Atropa, p. 288 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): flowers June-August; King's: May-August.

traits.fruiting_months.note: King's American Dispensatory (1898 text, 1905 printing), vol. 1, Belladonna, p. 331 (read on the Internet Archive, 2026-10-17): berries ripen in September.
